features.headline: The Connor McDavid Scoring Tracker: Can the Oilers' superstar break 200 points?
features.desc: Follow along game by game as No. 97 looks to break a benchmark that only No. 99 has done in NHL history.
body: There have been only four occasions in NHL history when a player scored 200 or more points in a single season, and only one player has accomplished the feat: Wayne Gretzky.
The Great One scored 215 points in 1985-86, 212 in '81-82, 208 in '84-85 and 205 in '83-84. Mario Lemieux came closest to Gretzky, finishing the '88-89 season with 199.
Connor McDavid plays for the same Edmonton Oilers franchise that Gretzky did when he posted those totals, and his personal best total is 153, set in 2022-23.
There are cases for and against McDavid breaking the 200-point barrier this season, as his pace fluctuates on a game-by-game basis.
Follow along below to monitor his pace after every game, along with highlights of memorable moments along the way.
Note that this page will be updated after each game, so come back to keep tabs on McDavid as the season continues.

features.headline: How Patriots' top 10 earners have fared: A.J. Brown, Christian Gonzalez, more
features.desc: The Patriots' 5-5 record reflects what happens when a team's highest-paid players don't perform well. Let's look closer at the top 10 earners in New England.
body: FOXBOROUGH, Mass. — Bang for the buck it is not.

The New England Patriots are 5-5 and reeling after two blowout losses that included a season-altering fibula injury to quarterback Drake Maye that is expected to sideline him deep into the regular season. One main reason why? The majority of their highest-paid players aren't producing.
The Patriots rank 11th in cash spending this year. They were ninth in 2025 and 15th in 2024. And the minimal return on investment is striking.

Mike Vrabel's team has a bye this week, providing an opportunity to step back and assess why the season hasn't unfolded as anticipated. Here is a deeper dive on the top 10 earners and their production.
Gonzalez was signed to a four-year, $135 million deal in September that made him the league's highest-paid cornerback in average per year.
But according to NFL Next Gen Stats, Gonzalez has allowed 12 receptions for 271 yards with three touchdowns and one interception over the past two games.
He had a missed tackle that contributed to Amon-Ra St. Brown's 56-yard tone-setting touchdown last Sunday, and it came after the Packers attacked him relentlessly the week prior.

"When your best players don't play good, you don't have much of a chance in this league. So, we expect a lot more. He expects a lot more," Vrabel said of Gonzalez after the Packers game. "We need more from him and everybody else. It wasn't just him.
Again, we got to be able to coach and be prepared, and then we have to execute. Just like it is every single week when we don't win, it's all of us, and it starts with me."

features.headline: Why the Jets' next two games have major implications on the 2027 draft
features.desc: At two wins, New York will play two of the three remaining one-win teams in Weeks 11 and 12.
body: LOS ANGELES — A look at what's happening around the New York Jets:
1. No tanks: It's the point in the season where the storyline turns into the "Bizarro" episode from the old "Seinfeld" series — a backward world in which up is down and down is up.
In this case, it's fans rooting for losses to improve draft position. It's an annual tradition in the Jets' universe, which hasn't seen a winning season since 2015.

Sunday and the following week will have a significant impact on the Jets' draft, as they face two teams in contention for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft — the Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) and the Miami Dolphins (1-8), both on the road.

If the Jets (2-8) beat the Chargers this Sunday at SoFi Stadium, their chances of landing the top pick would drop from 6% to 1%, according to ESPN Analytics. Their chances would jump to 8% with what would be their sixth straight loss.
The pro-tank crowd, disgusted by the results on the field, often roots blindly for losses, thinking the draft will be a panacea.

Since 2000, only four No. 1 picks have led their draft team to a Super Bowl — Joe Burrow, Jared Goff, Cam Newton and Eli Manning, the only one to win it all. (Technically, Manning wasn't picked by the Giants, but he was acquired in a draft-day trade.)

The consensus top prospect in the 2027 draft is a wide receiver, Jeremiah Smith, not a quarterback. While Drew Mestemaker has emerged as the top quarterback in most mock drafts, it's not like he's a slam-dunk, can't-miss pick.

So having the top pick is less important than in previous years. Armed with three first-round picks, the Jets should have the ability to trade up within the top 10 to land the quarterback they covet. They currently own the fourth, sixth (from Indianapolis) and 13th (from Dallas) picks.

features.headline: Falcons insist winning still the goal despite trading Jessie Bates III
features.desc: Atlanta wanted to ensure trading away Jessie Bates III didn't send the wrong message to the team.
body: FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — Overcommunication. That has been the order of business over the past several days for Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski.
That has included one-on-one meetings with players, small-group conversations with the team's player leadership committee and full team meetings.
Stefanski has wanted to make it absolutely certain that the Falcons, despite trading two starters before the NFL trade deadline earlier this week, are not in any way giving up on this season.

"I would tell you we've got a great group of leadership on this team," Stefanski said. "I've talked to them a lot over the last few days — like I do all the time, but in particular now. I'm very, very confident in their leadership."

On Monday, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Bates, aside from being arguably the best safety in the league, was also a team captain and one of the most respected veterans in the building.

A day later, Atlanta traded starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for reserve guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil was a Falcons success story, starting with the team as an undrafted free agent and working his way up to a starting role.

The Falcons are 3-6. So, in that respect, it made perfect sense to get value back for two players who were set to become free agents in the offseason. With regards to Bates, a safety had not been acquired for a second-round pick since 2018. Few could blame Atlanta for making the move.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddy Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
The New York Yankees and right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga are in agreement on a two-year deal with a club option for 2029, sources told ESPN, reuniting the reliever and club after a season apart.
Right-hander Troy Melton and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a six-year, $46.5 million contract extension, sources tell ESPN.
Outfielder Gavin Sheets and the San Diego Padres are in agreement on a three-year, $11 million contract, sources tell ESPN.

The Colorado Rockies are acquiring right-handers Davis Martin and Luis Castillo in a trade with the Chicago White Sox, sources tell ESPN. The White Sox are getting LHP Sean Sullivan and catching prospect Douglas Veliz in return.
Right-hander Randy Dobnak and the Kansas City Royals are in agreement on a one-year, $1.35 million contract, a source tells ESPN.
Right-hander Sonny Gray and the Minnesota Twins are in agreement on a two-year, the team announced. The contract is for $55 million and includes an opt-out after the first season, sources tell ESPN.

features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here, as this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.
The deals: David Bednar accepts one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer; Jonathan Loáisiga agrees to two-year, $18 million deal Grade: C+
Let's combine these two moves into one overall grade as the Yankees piece together the back end of their bullpen — a pen that ranked second in the majors with a 3.13 ERA in 2026.
The Yankees shoved Bednar into a corner by giving him a qualifying offer, which promised to limit his demand in free agency since he would have been tied to draft pick compensation.
By accepting it, Bednar's salary is now the highest average salary for a reliever, topping Edwin Diaz's $23 million with the Dodgers.

Other than a blip in 2024, Bednar has been steady since 2021, first with the Pirates and then with the Yankees after coming over at the trade deadline in 2025, posting sub-3.00 ERAs in five of his six seasons, including 2.47 ERA in 2026 when he racked up 35 saves in 39 opportunities.
He throws a four-seamer, splitter and curveball, with his splitter his big out pitch, holding batters to a.149 average in 2026 and.175 in 2025, with just one home run over the two seasons.
